links.reason: The Kural concerns openly honouring one's own spy (சிறப்பறிய ஒற்றின்கண் செய்யற்க); the epic's companions (தோழர்க்கு ... வேற்றுமை யின்றி) are guests being hidden, not spies, so the inverse is an analogy of concealment, not a limit on the couplet.

785 says no meeting is needed for friendship and 801 defines பழைமை as friendship that does not cut down liberties (கிழமையைக் கீழ்ந்திடா); the couplets make no incompatible claim. The teaches rests on a commentator's gloss, which the brief excludes.

1215 has the god foretell that a king will give his daughter (மகளைத் தந்து) and the friends will come; 1758 has Civakan report that a king gave his long-eyed daughter (நெடுங்கணாளைத் தந்தனன்). Prophecy and fulfilment; the archery fee in 1758 is a real addition the prophecy does not state.

875 describes the host passing through the sky (விசும்பு) and 948 orders them to walk the ground (நிலநடை படர்க); this is story sequence, and 'the aerial tour serves the protocol of a meeting' is not in either verse.
links.text_issue: 948 flagged uncertain; subject only 'he of the mountain'.

links.reason: Both tell the snake mistaking her face for the moon (மதி என்று தீண்ட / மதி யிதுவென் றெண்ணி), so scene expanding patikam is real. But teaches adds that she is reaching for a flower she raised; 1271 has no flower or reaching.

418 gives the saying மக்களை யிலாதவர் மரத்தொடு ஒப்ப and the king's praise of her wealth; it says nothing of a daughter's marriage prospect, which teaches and gains supply. Kural 61's அறிவறிந்த is not tested by this verse.

Both use falling fruit to urge acting now (காய்முதிர் கனியின் ஊழ்த்து வீழும் இவ்யாக்கை இன்னே; நற்காய் உதிர்தலும் உண்டு). But the epic's image is of sudden fall (இன்னே), not of death 'coming in order' as teaches says, and Naladiyar urges giving, not austerity.

46 foretells that the temple doors open at the son's foot (சரணத்தால் நீங்கும் திருக்கதவம்) with a pond; 51 shows the doors open at his foot's touch (சரணந் தீண்டக் ... கதவு நீங்க) and him falling into the flower pond. A clear sign and its fulfilment.

164 says the sage overcame harsh deeds (இறுகுவெவ் வினைகள் வென்று); Kural 5 says both deeds do not cling to those who praise the Lord. The verse is silent on any god, so 'through his own austerity and no god' is an argument from silence, and வெவ்வினை is not the couplet's two deeds.

Kalittokai 15 argues wealth recurs but youth does not (வளமையோ வைகலும் செயல் ஆகும் ... இளமையும் தருவதோ); Naladiyar 17 uses fallen fruit to warn against desiring a woman. They address different situations (a husband leaving for gain vs lust for another), so contrasting uses of the brevity of youth are not an incompatible claim.

868 posts two thousand sword-bearing maidens (வயிற்வாளர் ... புடை காத்தார்); 1344 has women tying the protective cord and worshipping (காப்புக் கட்டிச் சுற்றுபு தொழுது காத்தார்), a ritual guard. Only the general motif of women guarding a bride is shared.

1572 is the jester's reply to the king's rule in 1571 (வேதியர்க் கல்லால் ஈதல் இல்லை; வாதம் வல்லன்), so it is adjacent dialogue. The 'answer' is a joke, as the marker says; no development beyond the conversation.

1294 has Civakan stroke her whole body to hold her life (தைவந்தான்); 1342 cites that touch (ஆமெய் தீண்டி அளித்தனன்) and the maxim that women belong to the one who gained them (உற்றவர்க்கு உரியர்) as the ground of the match. The later verse recasts the cure as a claim, which neither shows alone.

1116's spider-thread simile (சிலம்பி நூலாற் சிமிழ்ப்புண்ட) names no parents; tying it to the embrace in 1138 (தந்தை புல்லி ... தோள் பிணிப்ப) relies on a reconstructed link of events. 'Lion held by a weak bond because he will not break his parents' hold' is inference.

1147 shows her recited spells bringing armed powers (விஞ்ஞை ... வாளும் வேலும்); 1709's verse does not name her, and shows only a vision (விளக்கிற்றன்றே), not sending his brother as the note says. A shared motif of spell-power, not an image.
links.text_issue: 1709 flagged uncertain; the woman is not named.

links.reason: 81 has women swoon after a dream prince; 476 has terrace women faint (மடந்தைமார் மயங்கினார்) as the procession passes, but nothing in 476 names the dream-prince. 'Fulfilment of the fear' needs the identification; the fear in 81 is that he will take their lives.

The king says யானே கள்வன் and prays கெடுக என் ஆயுள்; Kural 548 says the unexamining king தானே கெடும். It illustrates the couplet. But he wishes his end and falls rather than 'passing sentence', and 'easily approached' is not in these lines.

The god says the king never thought of him (முன் நினைத்தாயில்லை), so his help waits for a call, against Kural 788's friendship that clears distress at once (ஆங்கே இடுக்கண் களைவது). 'Silent through prison and war' is not in the verse, and the god-friend is a thin match for the couplet's human friend.

Devadattan says to find whether the lord lives or not and only then punish (ஆராய்ந்து ஒறுப்பதே), matching நாடி ... ஒறுப்பது. The domain shift from a king's judicial punishment to avenging subjects is real, but it is prudence in a speaker's mouth, not a definition of just punishment.

491's இன்பக் கடல் matches the Kural's இன்பம் கடல், a stock figure. 'Leaves out the greater pain because a wedding has no separation' is an argument from the verse's silence; the verse does not say there is no pain.

The king summons allies after the spy's report (ஒற்றன் உரைப்பக் கேட்டே ... வருகென); Kural 583 is about gathering and discerning through spies. The verse shows no weighing, so it illustrates only that a report is passed on; 'the report is the first step in the war' is not stated.

861 is an escort of armed women who guard her sides and bless her (புடை காப்ப ... பலாண்டு கூறி), not confinement; Kural 57 rejects the guard of confinement (சிறைகாக்கும் காப்பு). Calling the escort 'outward show' beside inward chastity is the pairing's judgment, not the verse's.

323 says only that the Dharma-heroes' leader speaks of life as a bondage of suffering and the audience hear it; it has no bubble image. 'Hearing is not yet the resolve' is invented from the unit's stopping point.

The time-keepers report elapsed ghatikas (கழிந்த நாழிகை) and bless the king; Kural 482 is about acting in accord with the season (பருவத்தோடு ஒட்ட ஒழுகல்). Reporting the hour is not knowing the season, and no link beyond 'time' is shown.

754 compares blossom among rocks to Indra's broken bow among dark clouds (இந்திரன் வின்முரிந்து இருண்முகில் வீழ்ந்த போலுமே); Akananuru 84 has the rainbow on the hill (மலைமிசை ... திருவில்) as the rain-season sign. The shared rainbow image is common and the uses differ only slightly.

The hunters apply the crocodile maxim (முதுநீர் முதலைக்கு வலிய துண்டேல் காட்டுண் அமக்கு வலியாரையும்) to themselves, restating 495's image. That the rule's limit shows in their defeat needs verse 453, not in this unit.
781 shows the dry omai forest under the sun; 795 shows the same country green and with peacocks (கார்மயிற் கலாபமொய்த்த கானக). Neither limits the other; it is a scene sequence on the road.

129 has Yugi resolve to part the king from the queen by trick (விரகினாற் பிரித்திடின்); 130 has him instruct an ascetic and paint a portrait. That is the plan starting, which the plot already records; 'the stratagem works through trust in others' is not stated.

355 reports the sage's word that 'he' will not be dazzled by kings' wealth and will reach சிவகதி by austerity; 2075 has the king resolve to strive for the final world (உலகெய்த முயல்வன்). The 'he' of 355 is not named, and 2075 shows no refusal of kings' wealth.

Thirikadugam names sloth while those bound hunger (பாசம் பசிப்ப மடியைக் கொளல்) as painful; Kural 603 has the sloth-bound fool's family perish before him. They share the harm of sloth to dependants; one does not extend the other, and the dependants reading of பாசம் is the marker's.

334 lists honouring teachers, learning and giving to ascetics as a path to release; Kural 222 says giving is good even if there is no higher world (மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும்), which does not deny a reward. They differ in motive, not in an incompatible claim.

1020 has the youth burn on seeing the picture of his beloved (கண்ணின் உருவம் கண்டே); Kural 1171 has the woman blame her eyes for showing her the sickness. The verse puts no guilt on the eyes, so 'the eyes' guilt is wider' is not shown.

304 has the kings pay tribute fearing his anger (செற்றவன் அலிதல் அஞ்சித் திறைகொடுத்து); Kural 680 concerns small domains bowing for what they can get. The minister's request to give the girl is not in 304, and the courtier's austerity claim in line 1 is the verse's main point.

The women say the mother must have done penance (செய்தவம் உடையள்) and ask which mountain, to attain too (எய்துவம் யாமும்), echoing 265's வேண்டிய ... எய்தலால் செய்தவம். What they wish to attain is open, so 'penance to win a man' and 'the couplet licenses it' are over-read.

295 says merit gathered brings sovereignty later (புண்ணியம் ஈண்டி மேல்வர); Kural 36 says virtue is the companion that does not perish at death (பொன்றாத் துணை). One is about reward in this life, the other about not deferring; neither limits the other.

257 has Madanan say he will not settle by mouth but by sword (வாளினால் பேசல் அல்லால் வாயினால் பேசல் தேற்றேன்); 2245 has him fall at the sword's edge (வாளின்வாய்). The wordplay is thin, and the next verses end the fight on an elephant's tusk, so 'answers his boast' overreads.

124 has the king spare the queen and her lover (வதையினுக் குரிய ரல்லர்); 154 has mourners say the queen killed her husband. The consequence is real, but the mourners blame her, not his sparing, and 124's reasons are sex and rank, so 'asks whether mercy was a fault' is not in the Tamil.

1057 sets spent good deeds and entering evil beside thickening darkness (நல்வினை கழிதலும் நலியும் தீவினை ... இருள் செறிந்து); Naladiyar 51's second half has darkness rushing in when oil is spent as evil stays when good deeds cease (நல்வினை தீர்விடத்து நிற்குமாம் தீது). The epic makes the figure the vehicle for night, reversing the quatrain.

The letter pledges life and invites him (தனக்கியா னுயிரு மீவேன் ... வருக), and the marker reads it as bait. The unit does not itself show it is menace; that depends on Govindan's laugh in 2148, which is outside it.

3145 has the Lord a moon rising from the sea of deeds (செய்வினை என்னும் முந்நீர்த் திரையிடை முளைத்து) and the poet praising his feet; it does not say the feet carry one across the sea as Kural 10 does. The sea of deeds against births is a real nuance, but the crossing claim is not in the verse.

1334 likens their joined love to the moon and its mark (திங்களும் மறுவும் எனச் சேர்ந்தது); Kural 1117 says her face has no spot like the moon. One image is used for different things, but there is no incompatible claim; the note also misdescribes 1334 as comparing a woman and her lover's view.

The Kural says the sea of love has no raft (ஏமப் புணை இல்); Kanakamalai swims the night-sea with the garland as raft (மாலை புணையாக யாமக் கடலை நீந்துவேன்). The shared words கடல், புணை and நீந்து make a real counter-case, and the sea is the night, not love, which is the limit teaches names.

3039 has the ascetics drop attachment and hatred like a snake's skin and shed the milk of kindness (தீம்பால் சுரந்தோம்பி); Kural 30 names brahmins by cool kindness to all lives. Both honour kindness, but the epic defines them by renunciation too, and 'not by robe or rite' is not in either text.
